title: Make macOS installation independent of fixed Homebrew library paths
scope: Fix the macOS release installation failure reported as `OutaskAI ./Install.command` followed by `Library not loaded: /opt/homebrew/opt/simdjson/lib/libsimdjson.33.dylib`. The report is one-off; no further information or testing can be requested from that user. Inspect the repository and release installation chain to identify and remove reliance on a developer machine's absolute Homebrew paths or a specific external dylib filename. Keep unnecessary third-party packages out of the repository/distribution. Detect required external programs through normal executable discovery, document and check their minimum supported versions, accept compatible newer versions, and offer installation guidance or an explicit installation action when a prerequisite is missing or too old. Homebrew must not be required merely because it was present on the build machine. Do not treat arbitrary native-library ABI versions as interchangeable or use dylib-name symlinks as a fix. Keep the scope to the macOS installer, its actual prerequisites and affected distribution checks/documentation.
acceptance: The shipped macOS installation/startup chain does not require /opt/homebrew/opt/simdjson/lib/libsimdjson.33.dylib or another developer-specific absolute third-party library path; record the identified source of the dependency, without claiming the unavailable user's environment was confirmed.

Required external programs are discovered independently of a single package-manager prefix. Their minimum supported versions are documented and checked; supported versions at or above the minimum proceed without requiring one exact package release.

Missing or too-old prerequisites produce a clear actionable message and an offer/instructions to install or upgrade before a dependent executable can fail with a raw loader error. Check the case where Homebrew itself is absent; do not silently require it or install software.

Verify the actual macOS archive on native Apple Silicon in an environment without the reported simdjson file: with supported prerequisites, run Install.command and an installed CLI/MCP smoke check successfully. Record evidence in this task; original reporter participation is not required.

Focused checks cover a missing prerequisite, a version below the minimum, the minimum supported version and a supported newer version, including discovery outside /opt/homebrew. Keep Linux and Windows installation contracts unchanged.
Update existing installation/prerequisite documentation to match the final behavior; do not add unnecessary bundled packages or promise compatibility with arbitrary native-library ABIs.

values.goal: Published archives support macOS Apple silicon with the documented runtime prerequisites.
values.value: Users can install and run Outask without reproducing the developer's Homebrew library layout or manually diagnosing a dyld error.
values.observable_result: The macOS archive installs and runs with supported discovered prerequisites; missing or outdated programs receive an actionable installation explanation.
values.verification: Native Apple Silicon archive installation and CLI/MCP smoke checks without libsimdjson.33.dylib, plus focused prerequisite discovery/version boundary checks.

notes: User approved task creation only, not implementation. The exact error is the only reporter evidence. Earlier discussion of how Homebrew entered the dependency chain is a hypothesis, not a verified diagnosis. Related completed task 1 addressed other installation issues; this task owns the newly reported fixed-library-path failure.
